items.title: Benjie White Interview, 1961-03-16
items.q: He was a piano player at the time with the Owls... Later, Moe's fair came in on the piano... The original Owls was composed of... and myself.

ctx.x: Harry Farrell, or we used to call him Moe's. Moe's Farrell. He was a piano player at the time with the Owls.
And it's at 2216 Pond Street, New Orleans, Louisiana.

items.title: Benjie White Interview, 1961-03-16
items.q: Later, Moe's fair came in on the piano and Red Mackey went to the bass... Moe's was with us at the Roosevelt Hotel

ctx.x: He's a, I think he's an architect here in town now. And Ogden was with the Bonds Department of one of the banks, I haven't seen him in years so I don't know what he's doing now. and Ogden was, was, well he wrote some of the funniest little pieces of music with words to it that, they were just cute pieces that's all and that was, as we used those to entertain the people at these two hotels over there. That was a forerunner to the, to the Owls. The original Owls was composed, the actual original Owls was composed…
You had a song on too.
